gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much energy Blink Solaris stores (3.2 V × 1.6 Ah = 5.12 Wh, LFP) or the average daily draw that Blink's 'up to one month without charging' claim works out to (5.12 Wh ÷ 30 days ≈ 0.17 Wh/day, about 7 mW on average).
standout_why: I compared against the cited Blink Solaris FAQ (en_US faq-blink-solaris) and the cited Solar Panel Mount FAQ, plus the US and UK Solaris FAQ copies that rank high. The Solaris FAQ gives 'up to one month' of power with no charging and '45 minutes of direct sunlight' a day. It gives no battery capacity, no Wh and no panel wattage. The Mount FAQ gives 11.84 Wh, but for the Outdoor (3rd Gen)-only mount, not for anything that fits the Outdoor 4. The Solaris capacity appears only on the Solaris Technical Specifications page, and ChatGPT never got that page (its rank-6 result is the Mount's spec page). No rival turns either figure into stored energy or a daily budget.
decides: This supports Solaris as the cable-free pick without settling it. It stores 5.12 Wh, which is 43% of the 11.84 Wh 18650 in Blink's older mount (5.12 ÷ 11.84). Blink sizes that buffer for about a month without sun at the camera's normal draw. A separately mounted panel only beats it on buffer if its internal battery holds more than about 5.1 Wh. I could not source the Wasserstein battery capacity or panel wattage, so that comparison can't be finished yet. The page should also flag that the Blink Solaris FAQ and Technical Specifications pages I opened name only the Outdoor 2K+ as compatible and never mention the Outdoor 4. Outdoor 4 compatibility rests on retailer titles such as Best Buy's 'Accessory for Outdoor 4 and Outdoor 2K+', and I could not open that page.

findings.label: Stored energy
findings.source_title: Blink Solaris Technical Specifications — Blink Support
findings.note: Spec: 'Rechargeable 3.2V 1600mAh LFP (Lithium Iron Phosphate) battery'. 3.2 V × 1.6 Ah = 5.12 Wh.

findings.label: Implied average camera draw from Blink's 'up to one month' claim
findings.note: FAQ: 'The rechargeable battery provides up to one month of power even when the camera is not charging.' 5.12 Wh ÷ 30 days = 0.171 Wh/day; ÷ 24 h = 7.1 mW. This is Blink's best case and assumes the full rated capacity can be used.

findings.label: Direct sun Blink says keeps it running
findings.note: 'Blink Solaris requires at least 45 minutes of direct sunlight daily for optimal performance.' To replace the ≈0.17 Wh/day draw in 45 min, the panel must average at least 0.171 Wh ÷ 0.75 h ≈ 0.23 W into the battery. Blink publishes no panel wattage.

findings.label: Weight per stored Wh
findings.source_title: Blink Solaris Technical Specifications — Blink Support
findings.note: Spec weight 5.5 oz (156 g). 156 g ÷ 5.12 Wh = 30.5 g/Wh. This weight hangs on the camera, because Solaris attaches directly to it. Other specs on the page: IP65, -22°F to 167°F, model BAS0430U.

findings.label: Compatibility stated on Blink's own Solaris pages
findings.note: The en_US, en_GB and helpjuice copies of the FAQ all read 'Blink Solaris is compatible with the Blink Outdoor 2K+.' The Technical Specifications page lists no cameras. ChatGPT's claim that Blink confirms Outdoor 4 support is not on these pages.

findings.label: Buffer in Blink's older Solar Panel Mount (Outdoor 3rd Gen only), for scale
findings.source_title: Blink Solar Panel Mount FAQ — Blink Support
findings.note: Mount FAQ: one 18650, '3.7 V, 3200mAh, 11.84Wh'; 'Outdoor 4, XT and XT2 not supported.' 5.12 ÷ 11.84 = 0.43.

findings.label: Camera's own power and rated life
findings.value: 2 × AA 1.5 V lithium, up to 2 years at default settings
findings.source_title: Blink Outdoor 4 Technical Specifications — Blink Support
findings.note: The spec page lists no USB port or input rating. It mentions only an optional 'Weather Resistant Power Adapter (sold separately)'. Operating range is -4 to 113°F, narrower than Solaris's own -22 to 167°F.
